_readme: Known-environment register: facts about the bank's own estate that the rules need (ranges, approved tools, critical systems). Values here override the defaults in app/config.py. status: assumed = invented for the prototype, confirmed = checked by the named owner. Change by pull request; an analyst who closes a case as false positive proposes the entry (see README: 'Learning the environment').

CORP_SOURCE_CIDRS.why: Corporate / VPN egress ranges. Cloud and token use from outside these is treated as suspicious.
CORP_SOURCE_CIDRS.source: Not known. 198.51.100.0/24 is a documentation placeholder.

APPROVED_LLM_HOSTS.why: LLM endpoints developers may use. Anything else receiving code or data is a policy breach (D5).

ALLOWED_EGRESS_SUFFIXES.why: Hosts an agent process may reach without a finding (package registries, source control, vendor docs).

TRUSTED_INSTALLERS.why: Vendor install scripts that may be piped to a shell. Others are high/critical (D4); these are low signals.
TRUSTED_INSTALLERS.source: Assumed: Docker, rustup, nvm, poetry, uv, bun, nodesource.

KNOWN_INSTALL_SCRIPTS.why: Public packages with a legitimate install script. New releases of these do not alert on 'new + install script'.

INTERNAL_REGISTRY_HOSTS.why: Internal package registries. An internal-looking name resolved elsewhere is dependency confusion (D3).

INTERNAL_PACKAGES.source: Sample names; replace from the registry inventory.

ORG_GIT_MARKERS.why: Remotes that belong to the bank. A push elsewhere is a copy-out (D7).
ORG_GIT_MARKERS.source: Assumed GitHub org nb-bank plus internal hosts.

PROTECTED_BRANCHES.why: Branches where force-push or direct rewrite is a finding. Exact names or globs.

EXPECTED_SECRET_READERS.why: Identities that legitimately read secrets at deploy time (not a D10 burst).

CRITICAL_REPOS.why: Repos that raise a case's priority (payments, ledger, risk).

CRITICAL_HOSTS.why: Host-name prefixes that raise priority (CI runners).

THIRD_PARTY_USER_PREFIX.why: User-name prefix of third-party developers on unmanaged devices.

value: Developer VDI subnet for third-party developers
Production network: no agent or developer-laptop access
Internet: only via the egress proxy, DNS via the corporate resolver
used_by: documentation only (not read by a rule yet)
NETWORK_ZONES.why: Where traffic comes from and goes to. Drives CORP_SOURCE_CIDRS and the egress and DNS allow-lists, and the architecture diagram.
NETWORK_ZONES.source: Assumed zones; the real network design is not known.

value: Employees: SSO + MFA, then VPN/ZTNA to GitHub, registries and the gateways
Third-party developers: VDI only, no local source code, same gateways
Coding agents: reach models only through the LLM gateway and tools only through the MCP gateway
CI runners: pull packages through the registry proxy, cloud access by assumed role
used_by: documentation only (not read by a rule yet)
ACCESS_PATHS.why: How people and agents reach code, models and cloud. Decides which gateways can see what.
ACCESS_PATHS.source: Assumed: SSO+MFA, VPN/ZTNA, VDI for third parties, gateway-only agents.

value: Agent identity: short-lived agent_token issued per session and bound to the developer
Service identity: svc-* accounts and assumed roles (svc-ci)
used_by: documentation only (not read by a rule yet)
IDENTITY_TYPES.why: Human, third-party, agent and service identities and how they are named. Rules use the ext. prefix; others are used by runbooks.

used_by: documentation only (not read by a rule yet)
AGENT_INVENTORY.why: The coding agents in use. An agent not on this list is shadow AI.

value: IDE/agent telemetry: vendor hook or extension, via the log shipper
Shell: auditd / EDR on managed laptops and runners
LLM and MCP gateways: gateway access logs
Egress proxy and DNS resolver logs
Package audit: registry proxy and CI
Identity provider: sign-in and token events
Log shipper heartbeats every 5 minutes (liveness of every endpoint)
used_by: documentation only (not read by a rule yet)
LOG_COLLECTION_PATHS.why: How each log source reaches the SIEM. Drives the telemetry-health view and the day-one availability in the architecture.

value: SOC on-call: first responder (MDR L2 hands over here)
DPO / Compliance: customer-data exposure and regulator notification (CBUAE)
Cloud security: cloud keys and logging
AppSec: rules files, MCP servers, packages
Engineering lead: repository owner, history rewrite
used_by: documentation only (not read by a rule yet)
ESCALATION_ROLES.why: Who is called for what. Runbooks name roles, not people.
ESCALATION_ROLES.source: Assumed roles; replace with real on-call rota and names.

SOC_AI_ENDPOINTS.why: The only endpoints the optional SOC AI assistant may call. Anything else is refused before any data is sent.
SOC_AI_ENDPOINTS.source: Assumed: the bank's internal LLM gateway. The assistant is off by default.
